facts.statement: The --setup-show command-line option is registered as a boolean option whose stated purpose is to show fixture setup while tests execute.

During fixture setup with setup display enabled, pytest saves either a callable-generated ID, an indexed explicit ID, or the raw request parameter in fixturedef.cached_param before showing the setup action.
The setup-action renderer writes cached_param using "[{}]".format(fixturedef.cached_param), which invokes ordinary string formatting on the parameter value.
The same setup-action renderer is called for teardown while cached_param still exists, and cached_param is deleted only after the teardown action is shown.
The repository defines saferepr as a size-limited representation helper intended to handle failing __repr__ implementations without generally raising exceptions.
Existing setup-display tests are parameterized across --setup-only, --setup-plan, and --setup-show.
Existing parameter-display coverage uses string fixture parameters 'foo' and 'bar' and expects those values in both setup and teardown output.
Existing explicit-ID coverage uses string parameters with string IDs and verifies the IDs 'spam' and 'ham' in setup output.
Existing callable-ID coverage transforms string parameters to uppercase string IDs and verifies those IDs in setup output.

scope_summary: Inspected base commit 5e7f1ab4bf58e473e5d7f878eb2b499d7deabd29. The existing setup-display path stores raw parameter values when no explicit ID is available and interpolates them with normal string formatting; the repository already provides a safe representation helper, while current setup-display tests cover textual parameters and IDs.
